Lesson 1.1.18

Fairs, Festivals, Puppetry & Cultural Heritage

In this lessonDetailed StudyRevision DigestKey Points & MindmapDiagrams, Maps & FlowchartsPrevious Year Questions

Detailed Study

The full treatment of this lesson.

Anchor facts only: where, when, why, and the UNESCO-intangible list. Prelims loves state-festival mismatch.

1. Kumbh Mela

  • 4 sites rotation: Haridwar (Ganga), Prayagraj (sangam), Ujjain (Shipra — Simhastha), Nashik (Godavari); 12-year cycle + ardha/magh variants; UNESCO ICH 2017; akhara processions (shahi snan procession order); 2019 Prayagraj largest gathering record.

2. Regional festival anchors

  • Harvest trio: Pongal (TN, Jan — Thai month; Mattu day), Baisakhi/Lohri/Maghi (Punjab — Khalsa founding 1699 hook), Bihu (Assam — Bohag magh kati trio; Rongali = spring).
  • South: Onam (Kerala — Mahabali-Vamana; pookalam, snake-boat Vallam Kali), Thrissur Pooram (Sakthan Thampuran origin), Hampi Utsav, Pongal-adjacent Mattu Pongal.
  • East: Durga Puja (WB — UNESCO ICH 2021), Chhath (Bihar-Jharkhand — Surya-Shashthi, Kartik), Rath Yatra (Puri — 3 chariots; Jagannath, Balabhadra, Subhadra), Ambubachi Mela (Kamakhya, Assam — tantric, temple closes).
  • North: Hornbill Festival (Nagaland Dec-1 — 'festival of festivals', tribal unity), Losar (Ladakh-Arunachal, Tibetan new year), Baisakhi hook, Gangaur-Teej (Rajasthan — Gauri), Makar Sankranti family (Uttarayan Gujarat kites, Magh Bihu, Poush Sankranti Bengal, Suggi Karnataka).
  • West: Pushkar Fair (Kartik, camel trade), Shigmo (Goa spring), Gudi Padwa (Maharashtra new year), Modhera dance festival (Sun temple).
  • NE-tribal: Chapchar Kut (Mizoram), Wangala (Garo — 100-drum), Moatsu (Ao Naga), Sarhul (Jharkhand tribal spring), Nuakhai (Odisha new rice).

3. Fair classics (commodity + faith)

  • Pushkar (Rajasthan — camels, Brahma temple), Sonepur (Bihar — cattle+elephants, Harihar Kshetra), Surajkund Mela (Haryana — crafts, Feb), Hemis (Ladakh — Guru Padmasambhava mask), Gangasagar (WB Makar Sankranti), Nauchandi (Meerut), Bateshwar (UP cattle fair), Shamlaji (Gujarat tribal).

4. UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage — India

  • Kutiyattam (2001), Vedic chanting (2003), Ramlila (2005), Ramman (Uttarakhand, 2009), Mudiyettu (Kerala, 2010), Chhau (2010), Kalbelia (2010), Buddhist chanting of Ladakh (2012), Sankirtana (Manipur, 2013), Traditional brass/utensil craft of Thatheras (Punjab, 2014 — only craft), Yoga (2016), Nawrouz (multinational, 2016), Kumbh Mela (2017), Kolkata Durga Puja (2021), Garba of Gujarat (2023). Chronology asked directly.

MCQ hooks

  • 4 Kumbh cities + rivers pair (Shipra-Ujjain, Godavari-Nashik).
  • Thatheras = only craft on the ICH list (2014).
  • Hornbill = Dec 1, Nagaland; Chapchar Kut = Mizoram.
  • Ambubachi = Kamakhya closure, not open darshan.
  • Onam snake-boats = Vallam Kali (Aranmula).
  • Durga Puja 2021 & Garba 2023 = latest India adds.

Part I — GS Paper I — General Studies (Prelims) · Chapter 1: History & Indian Culture

Lesson 1.1.19

Scriptures, Languages & Literature

In this lessonDetailed StudyRevision DigestKey Points & MindmapDiagrams, Maps & FlowchartsPrevious Year Questions

Detailed Study

The full treatment of this lesson.

Three chains: scripts (Indus → Brahmi → derivatives), language families (Indo-Aryan/Dravidian/Austro-Asiatic/Tibeto-Burman), and the scripture corpora per faith.

1. Scripts

  • Indus: c.2600-1900; sign-count ~375-400; undeciphered; direction debated (right-to-left majority view), boustrophedon on some seals.
  • Brahmi: Ashokan 3rd c BCE, first deciphered 1837 by James Prinsep); written left-to-right; parent of Devanagari, Tamil-Brahmi, Kannada-Telugu, Bengali-Assamese, Odia, Gujarati, Sinhala, Tibetan lineages.
  • Kharosthi: NW (Gandhara), right-to-left, Aramaic-derived; dies ~3rd c CE; Gandhari Prakrit + Kharosthi manuscripts (Buddhist, found as Gandhara birch-bark scrolls).
  • Evolution mnemonic: Brahmi → Gupta script → Siddham → Devanagari (c.11th); southern: Tamil-Brahmi → Vatteluttu & Tamil.

2. Languages & literature

  • Indo-Aryan: Vedic Sanskrit → Classical (Panini's Ashtadhyayi codifies); epics (Ramayana — Valmiki; Mahabharata — Vyasa; Gita inside); Puranas (18 mahapuranas); darshanas (6 schools); Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit (Lalitavistara); Prakrits: Magadhi (Jain Ardhamagadhi Agamas), Shauraseni, Maharashtri (Gathasaptashati, Hala), Paisachi (Brihatkatha, Gunadhya); Pali: Tipitaka (Vinaya-Sutta-Abhidhamma), Milindapanha, Dipavamsa-Mahavamsa.
  • Apabhramsa → modern IA: Prithviraj Raso (Chand Bardai), Jain narrative verse; Hindi branch: Avadhi (Ramcharitmanas — Tulsidas), Braj (Sursagar), Khari Boli (Rasos, later Urdu-Hindi).
  • Dravidian: Tamil (Tolkappiyam; Sangam anthologies: Ettuthogai + Pattuppattu; Pathinenkilkanakku (18 works) incl. Tirukkural); Telugu (Nannaya Mahabharata start), Kannada (Pampa, Ponna, Ranna — 'ratnatraya'), Malayalam (Manipravalam blend; Tunchath Ezhuthachan (Adhyatma Ramayanam)).
  • Urdu: Khari Boli + Persian script (Nastaliq); Amir Khusrau early; Deccani branch (Ibrahim Adil Shah II's Kitab-i-Nauras); ghazal-masnavi forms; Ghalib-Iqbal-Faiz line.
  • Others: Santali (Austro-Asiatic), Manipuri/Meitei (Tibeto-Burman; ancient script suppressed-revived), Bodo, Dogri, Santhali — 8th Schedule now 22 languages; classical-language tag: Tamil, Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia, + Marathi/Pali-Prakrit/Assamese/Bengali (2024 round — VERIFY current list each attempt).

3. Scripture corpora (pair faith → canon)

  • Hindu: Shruti (4 Vedas + Brahmanas + Aranyakas + Upanishads) vs Smriti (epics, dharmashastras — Manusmriti, nibandhas); Vedas: Rig (hymns, 10 mandalas), Yajus (Yajur — prose ritual), Sama (melodic — rig-based), Atharva (folk-magic); each Veda has shakhas (recensions).
  • Buddhist: Tipitaka; Mahayana add: Prajnaparamita, Saddharma Pundarika; Tibetan Kangyur-Tengyur; Pali commentaries (Buddhaghosa — Visuddhimagga).
  • Jain: Agamas (Angas-Upangas; Shvetambara canon vs Digambara loss-claim); Tattvartha Sutra (Umasvati — accepted by both); Kalpasutra (Bhadrabahu).
  • Sikh: Adi Granth (Arjan, 1604) → Guru Granth Sahib (Gobind Singh, 1708); Dasam Granth separate; Janamsakhis = Nanak biographies.

MCQ hooks

  • Prinsep = 1837 Brahmi decipherment; Kharosthi = right-to-left.
  • Gathasaptashati = Hala (Maharashtri); Brihatkatha = Gunadhya (Paisachi).
  • Adi Granth 1604 by Guru Arjan; installed Harmandir; final Guru 1708.
  • Tattvartha Sutra = both Jain sects accept; Visuddhimagga = Buddhaghosa.
  • Tolkappiyam = oldest Tamil grammar; Tirukkural = Tiruvalluvar.
  • Ashtadhyayi = Panini (~500 BCE?); 'shabdanushasana' = Chandragomin (Buddhist grammar rival).
studyUPSC · print-friendly (Ctrl/Cmd+P)

Revision Digest

Condensed for the last mile before the exam.

Prelims GS-I › History & Culture › Art & Culture. Text–author–language matching and the Eighth Schedule/classical language list.

Religious & philosophical texts

  • Vedic corpus (see Vedic card): Samhitas → Brahmanas → Aranyakas → Upanishads; Vedangas; Sutras (Shrauta, Grihya, Dharma — Gautama, Baudhayana, Apastamba, Vasishtha); Smritis — Manusmriti (c. 200 BCE–200 CE), Yajnavalkya (Mitakshara by Vijnaneshvara; Dayabhaga — Jimutavahana, Bengal), Narada, Parashara.
  • Epics: Mahabharata (Vyasa; 18 parvas; Jaya 8,800 → Bharata 24,000 → 1,00,000 shatasahasri samhita; Bhagavad Gita in Bhishma parva, 18 chapters, 700 shlokas), Ramayana (Valmiki; 7 kandas; 24,000 verses; adikavya).
  • Puranas (18 Maha; pancha-lakshana — sarga, pratisarga, vamsha, manvantara, vamshanucharita; Vishnu, Bhagavata, Matsya (oldest), Vayu, Markandeya (Devi Mahatmya), Agni, Garuda, Skanda (largest)).
  • Buddhist: Pali Tripitaka; Jatakas (547), Dhammapada, Milindapanho, Mahavamsa/Dipavamsa (Sri Lanka), Sanskrit — Lalitavistara, Buddhacharita, Saundarananda (Ashvaghosha), Mahavastu, Divyavadana, Nagarjuna Mulamadhyamakakarika, Vasubandhu Abhidharmakosha, Shantideva Bodhicharyavatara, Dignaga/Dharmakirti (logic).
  • Jain: 12 Angas, 12 Upangas, Prakirnas, Chhedasutras, Mulasutras (Ardha-Magadhi); Kalpasutra (Bhadrabahu), Tattvartha Sutra (Umaswati — both sects), Acharanga, Bhagavati Sutra; Kannada — Adipurana (Jinasena/Pampa), Vikramarjuna Vijaya.
  • Sikh: Guru Granth Sahib (Adi Granth 1604 Guru Arjan; Bhai Gurdas scribe; 1430 angs; 31 ragas; Bhagat bani — Kabir, Namdev, Ravidas, Farid; Guru Gobind Singh added Tegh Bahadur's hymns 1705 Damdama; Guru 1708), Dasam Granth, Janamsakhis.
  • Bhakti/Sufi: Alvars (12; Nalayira Divya Prabandham — Nathamuni; Andal Tiruppavai), Nayanars (63; Tevaram; Periya Puranam — Sekkizhar; Tirumurai 12; Manikkavachakar Tiruvachakam), Shankara (Advaita; Brahmasutra bhashya; 4 mathas), Ramanuja (Vishishtadvaita; Sri Bhashya), Madhva (Dvaita), Nimbarka (Dvaitadvaita), Vallabha (Shuddhadvaita; Pushtimarg), Basavanna (Vachanas; Lingayat/Virashaiva; Anubhava Mantapa; Akka Mahadevi), Jnaneshwar (Jnaneshwari 1290; Marathi), Namdev, Eknath, Tukaram (abhang), Ramdas (Dasbodh), Kabir (Bijak; doha), Ravidas, Nanak, Chaitanya (Gaudiya; sankirtana), Shankaradeva (Borgeet, Kirtan Ghosha; Ekasarana), Mirabai, Surdas (Sursagar), Tulsidas (Ramcharitmanas 1574, Awadhi; Hanuman Chalisa), Narsi Mehta (Vaishnava jana to), Dadu, Malik Muhammad Jayasi (Padmavat 1540, Awadhi), Amir Khusrau, Bulleh Shah, Sultan Bahu, Shah Latif (Risalo), Lal Ded (Kashmir vakhs), Nund Rishi (Sheikh Noor-ud-din).

Secular classics

  • Grammar/lexicon: Panini Ashtadhyayi (c. 4th BCE; 4,000 sutras), Katyayana Varttika, Patanjali Mahabhashya, Amarasimha Amarakosha, Tolkappiyam (Tamil grammar; earliest).
  • Polity/economy: **Kautilya *Arthashastra*** (15 adhikaranas; rediscovered Shamasastry 1905, published 1909), Kamandaka Nitisara, Shukra Nitisara, Somadeva Nitivakyamrita.
  • Science: Aryabhata (Aryabhatiya 499), Varahamihira (Brihat Samhita, Pancha-siddhantika, Brihat Jataka), Brahmagupta (Brahmasphutasiddhanta 628; zero rules), Bhaskara I, Bhaskara II (Siddhanta Shiromani 1150 — Lilavati, Bijaganita), Madhava of Sangamagrama (Kerala school; series), Nilakantha (Tantrasangraha), Charaka & Sushruta Samhitas, Vagbhata (Ashtanga Hridaya), Nagarjuna (Rasaratnakara), Kanada (atomism), Lagadha (Vedanga Jyotisha), Sulba sutras (Baudhayana — "Pythagoras").
  • Drama/kavya: Bhasa, Kalidasa, Shudraka, Vishakhadatta, Bhavabhuti, Harsha (Nagananda, Ratnavali, Priyadarshika), Bana (Harshacharita, Kadambari), Dandin (Dashakumaracharita, Kavyadarsha), Subandhu (Vasavadatta), Magha (Shishupalavadha), Bharavi (Kiratarjuniya), Sriharsha (Naishadhiyacharita), Bilhana (Vikramankadevacharita), Kalhana (Rajatarangini 1148–50 — Kashmir; first "history"), Somadeva (Kathasaritsagara), Jayadeva (Gita Govinda), Kshemendra, Vatsyayana (Kamasutra), Bhartrihari (Shatakatraya), Vishnu Sharma (Panchatantra), Narayana (Hitopadesha), Vetala Panchavimshati, Brihatkatha (Gunadhya).
  • Tamil Sangam: three sangams (Madurai); Ettutogai (8 anthologies), Pattuppattu (10 idylls), Padinenkilkanakku (18 minor; Tirukkural — Tiruvalluvar; 1,330 couplets; aram, porul, inbam), epics — Silappadikaram (Ilango; Kannagi), Manimekalai (Sattanar; Buddhist), Jivaka Chintamani (Tiruttakkadevar; Jain), Valayapathi, Kundalakesi; Kamba Ramayanam (12th c.); Nakkirar, Kapilar, Avvaiyar.
  • Other regional firsts: Kannada — Kavirajamarga (Amoghavarsha/Srivijaya, 9th c.), Pampa-Ponna-Ranna (ratnatraya), Telugu — Nannaya (Andhra Mahabharatam; adikavi), Tikkana, Errana (kavitraya); Malayalam — Ramacharitam, Ezhuthachan (Adhyatma Ramayanam; father of Malayalam), Cherusseri; Odia — Sarala Das (Mahabharata), Jagannatha Das (Bhagabata), Balarama Das; Bengali — Charyapada (oldest; Buddhist siddhas, 8th–12th), Krittibas (Ramayana), Kashiram Das, Chandidas, Mukundaram (Chandimangal), Bharatchandra; Assamese — Madhava Kandali (14th c. Ramayana), Shankaradeva; Marathi — Jnaneshwari, Mahanubhava panth (Lilacharitra), Leelacharitra; Hindi — Prithviraj Raso, Amir Khusrau (Khaliq Bari), Kabir, Jayasi, Tulsi, Sur, Bihari (Satsai), Keshavdas; Punjabi — Farid, Nanak, Waris Shah (Heer 1766), Bulleh Shah; Urdu — Amir Khusrau (proto), Quli Qutb Shah (first diwan), Wali Dakhani, Mir, Sauda, Ghalib, Zauq, Momin, Iqbal (Tarana-e-Hind 1904, Bang-e-Dara); Persian — Barani, Abul Fazl, Faizi, Badauni, Dara (Majma-ul-Bahrain), Khafi Khan (Muntakhab-ul-Lubab).
  • Modern: Bankim (Anandamath 1882 — Vande Mataram; Durgeshnandini first Bengali novel 1865), Michael Madhusudan (Meghnad Badh Kavya; blank verse), Tagore (Gitanjali 1910; Nobel 1913; Jana Gana Mana 1911 Calcutta Congress; Amar Sonar Bangla; Gora, Ghare Baire), Premchand (Godan, Nirmala; Soz-e-Watan banned 1909), Bharatendu Harishchandra (Andher Nagari; father of modern Hindi), Subramania Bharati, Bharatidasan, Kumaran Asan, Vallathol, Kuvempu, Bendre, Karanth, Mahadevi Verma, Nirala, Pant, Prasad (Chhayavad), Iqbal, Faiz, Manto, Sarat Chandra (Devdas, Pather Dabi banned), Fakir Mohan Senapati (Chha Mana Atha Guntha), Gopinath Mohanty, Lakshminath Bezbaroa, O. Chandu Menon (Indulekha 1889), Gurajada Apparao (Kanyasulkam), Viresalingam; Jnanpith (1965; first G. Sankara Kurup; 2023 Gulzar & Rambhadracharya; 2024 Vinod Kumar Shukla); Sahitya Akademi awards 24 languages.

Languages & scripts

  • Eighth Schedule: 22 languages (14 original + Sindhi 1967 (21st Amdt) + Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali 1992 (71st) + Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santali 2003 (92nd)); English is not in it; Hindi in Devanagari official (Art 343); Official Languages Act 1963; Classical 11 (see fairs card).
  • Families: Indo-Aryan (~78%), Dravidian (~20%; Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Tulu, Gondi, Brahui (Balochistan), Kurukh, Malto), Austro-Asiatic (Munda — Santali (Ol Chiki script, Raghunath Murmu 1925), Ho, Mundari, Kharia; Khasi; Nicobarese), Tibeto-Burman (Bodo, Manipuri/Meitei — Meitei Mayek, Mizo, Naga groups, Lepcha, Ladakhi), Tai-Kadai (Ahom, Khamti), Great Andamanese, Ongan; Census 2011 — 121 languages, 19,569 raw mother tongues, 22 scheduled speakers 96.7%.
  • Scripts: Brahmi (Ashokan; mother of all Indic; Prinsep 1837), Kharosthi (right-to-left; NW; Aramaic-derived; died 3rd c. CE), Gupta → Siddham/Nagari → Devanagari; Sharada (Kashmir), Grantha (Tamil Sanskrit), Vatteluttu (early Tamil), Tamil-Brahmi (Keezhadi finds 6th BCE claim), Kadamba-Chalukya → Kannada-Telugu, Modi (Marathi), Gurmukhi (Guru Angad standardised), Ol Chiki, Meitei Mayek, Tolong Siki (Kurukh), Wancho, Sorang Sompeng (Sora), Tigalari, Takri (Dogri), Landa (Sindhi/Punjabi mercantile), Nastaliq (Urdu), Sylheti Nagri; Indus script undeciphered.
  • Language policy hooks: Three-language formula (Kothari 1968; NEP 2020 flexible), Art 350A (mother tongue primary), 350B (Special Officer for linguistic minorities), Art 351 (Hindi development), Bhasha Sangam, Bharatavani portal, NTM (translation), Scheme for Protection of Endangered Languages (SPPEL — CIIL Mysuru; 117 languages <10,000 speakers), PM e-VIDYA, Bhashini (AI translation); UNESCO Atlas — 197 Indian languages endangered; Census 2011 non-scheduled 99 languages (Bhili largest, ~1.04 crore).

Traps

  • Tirukkural is part of Padinenkilkanakku (post-Sangam), not Ettutogai.
  • Kharosthi is right-to-left; Brahmi left-to-right; both on Ashokan records.
  • 22 scheduled languages ≠ 11 classical (Pali & Prakrit are classical but not scheduled; Sindhi, Nepali, Bodo etc. are scheduled but not classical).
  • Vande Mataram is from Anandamath (1882; song composed 1875); Jana Gana Mana first sung Dec 1911.

Match-drills.

Script flash

  • Indus → undeciphered, ~400 signs · Brahmi → Prinsep 1837, L-to-R · Kharosthi → NW, R-to-L, Aramaic kin.
  • Devanagari line → Brahmi → Gupta → Siddham · Tamil line → Tamil-Brahmi → Vatteluttu.
  • Gandhari manuscripts → Kharosthi birch-bark (Buddhist).

Language flash

  • Gathasaptashati → Hala, Maharashtri · Brihatkatha → Gunadhya · Milindapanha → Pali.
  • Ashtadhyayi → Panini · shabdanushasana → Chandragomin.
  • Avadhi → Tulsidas Ramcharitmanas · Braj → Surdas · Nastaliq → Urdu.
  • Manipravalam → Malayalam-Sanskrit blend · Ezhuthachan → Malayalam father-figure.
  • Classical tags → Tamil first (2004), then Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia (+ recent adds — re-verify).

Scripture flash

  • Shruti vs Smriti → heard vs remembered corpora · 4 Vedas → Rig-Yajur-Sama-Atharva.
  • Tipitaka → Vinaya-Sutta-Abhidhamma · Visuddhimagga → Buddhaghosa · Kangyur-Tengyur → Tibetan.
  • Jain Agamas → Shvetambara canon · Tattvartha Sutra → Umasvati (both sects) · Kalpasutra → Bhadrabahu.
  • Adi Granth → Guru Arjan 1604 · Guru Granth Sahib → 1708 Gobind Singh · Janamsakhi → Nanak life tales.

Trap flash

  • Pali ≠ Prakrit family label games: Pali = Tipitaka language; Ardhamagadhi = Jain canon.
  • Sama Veda melodies derive from Rig hymns — not independent text.
  • Vatteluttu ≠ Tamil-Brahmi (parallel southern script).
  • Urdu script = Nastaliq Persian form, NOT Arabic Kufic.

Chapter 1.2 — Geography

Part I — GS Paper I — General Studies (Prelims) · Chapter 2: Geography

Lesson 1.2.1

Geomorphology: Earth, Landforms & Rocks

In this lessonDetailed StudyRevision DigestKey Points & MindmapDiagrams, Maps & FlowchartsPrevious Year Questions

Detailed Study

The full treatment of this lesson.

Interior, plate tectonics, earthquakes-volcanoes, and the four erosional agents. Statement-true/false territory.

1. Earth's interior

  • Layers: crust (continental ~35-70 km vs oceanic ~5-10 km; SIAL-SIMA terminology legacy), mantle (to ~2900 km; upper asthenosphere = partial-melt, plate lubricant), core (outer liquid, inner solid — Fe-Ni). Discontinuities: Conrad (crust-internal), Moho (crust-mantle), Repetti (mantle-internal), Gutenberg (mantle-core), Lehmann (inner core).
  • Evidence: direct (mining, drilling — deepest Kola ~12 km) vs indirect (seismic P-S wave shadow zones, meteorites density, isostasy — Airy vs Pratt).

2. Plate tectonics

  • Theory chain: continental drift (Wegener 1912: Pangaea-Panthalassa, jigsaw-fit, Glossopteris flora evidence) → sea-floor spreading (Hess 1961; palaeomagnetic stripes, youngest-at-ridge) → plate tectonics (1960s; 7 major plates: Pacific largest; Indian plate split from Gondwana, NE-drift ~5-6 cm/yr).
  • Boundaries: divergent (mid-Atlantic ridge, East African rift), convergent (ocean-continent: Andes; ocean-ocean: Japan arc; continent-continent: Himalaya), transform (San Andreas). Hotspots: Hawaii chain (intra-plate volcanism), Reunion-Deccan linkage (K-T flood basalt ~66 Ma).

3. Earthquakes & volcanoes

  • Earthquake terms: focus-hypocentre, epicentre, seismograph; Richter magnitude vs Mercalli intensity; waves P (fastest, all media) S (solids only) L/R (surface, most destructive). India seismic zones: II-V (zone V: Himalaya-NE-Rann-Kutch-Andaman).
  • Volcano types: shield (Mauna Loa), composite-strato (Fuji, Andes), cinder, caldera (Krakatoa), flood-basalt (Deccan); extrusive landforms (cone-crater-lava plateau) vs intrusive (batholith, laccolith, lopolith, phacolith, sill-dyke). Distribution: Pacific Ring of Fire (~2/3 of world volcanoes), mid-Atlantic, East African rift. Barren Island = India's only active volcano.

4. Erosional agents & landforms

  • Fluvial: youth (V-valleys, gorges, waterfalls) → maturity (meanders) → old (oxbow lakes, deltas — arcuate/bird-foot/estuarine); peneplain concept. Arid: deflation-hollows, mushroom rocks, yardangs-zeugen, inselberg-playa; loess (wind-blown, China). Glacial: cirque-horn-arete (erosion), moraine-drumlins-eskers (deposition), U-valleys, fjords. Coastal: cliffs-wave-cut platforms, beaches-spits-bars, lagoons; Karst (groundwater): sinkholes, caves-stalactites-stalagmites.
  • India anchors: Himalaya (Siwalik-Lesser-Great-Karakoram-Ladakh ranges; syntaxial bends), Peninsular block stability, Deccan Traps, Western vs Eastern Ghats asymmetry, coastal plains (Konkan-Malabar vs Utkal-Coromandel), islands (Andaman-Nicobar extension of Arakan-Yoma; Lakshadweep coral atolls).

MCQ hooks

  • Moho = crust-mantle; Gutenberg = mantle-core; shadow zones = liquid outer core proof.
  • Sea-floor spreading youngest-at-ridge; Hess; palaeomagnetism evidence.
  • Zone-V list = Himalayan arc (J&K, HP, Uttarakhand) + NE states + Kutch + Andaman-Nicobar; Bihar is zone IV.
  • Barren Island active; Narcondam dormant.
  • Esker = glacial-fluvial deposit ridge; loess = wind.
  • Himalaya = continent-continent convergence; Andes = ocean-continent.

Revision Digest

Condensed for the last mile before the exam.

Prelims GS-I › Geography › Physical Geography. Concept-definition questions (which landform is formed by X?) plus earth-interior facts.

Earth's interior

  • Layers: crust (continental sial 30–70 km, oceanic sima 5–10 km; Conrad discontinuity between) → Mohorovičić (Moho) → mantle (to 2,900 km; asthenosphere 100–200 km partially molten; Repetti 700 km) → Gutenberg → outer core (liquid; no S-waves; nife) → Lehmann → inner core (solid; 5,150–6,371 km).
  • Evidence: seismic waves — P (longitudinal, all media, fastest), S (transverse, solids only; shadow zone 105°–145° for S entirely beyond 105°; P shadow 105°–145°), L/R surface waves (most destructive). Density 2.7 crust → 13 core; temperature ~5,500 °C core.
  • Earthquakes: focus/hypocentre & epicentre; scales — Richter (magnitude, log₁₀; energy ×31.6 per unit), Mercalli (intensity I–XII), Moment magnitude (Mw — now standard). India seismic zones II–V (V: Kashmir, HP, Uttarakhand, Bihar-Nepal, NE, Kutch, Andaman); Bureau of Indian Standards IS 1893. Tsunami: shallow-focus subduction quakes (2004 Sumatra 9.1).
  • Volcanoes: shield (Hawaii; basaltic), composite/strato (Fuji, Vesuvius; andesitic), caldera (Toba, Crater Lake), flood basalt (Deccan Traps; Siberian), mid-ocean ridge; India: Barren Island (only active; Andaman), Narcondam (dormant); Ring of Fire; VEI; lava — pahoehoe/aa; intrusive forms: batholith, laccolith, lopolith, phacolith, sill, dyke.

Plate tectonics & continental drift

  • Wegener 1912 (Pangaea, Panthalassa; Laurasia/Gondwana; Tethys; evidence: jigsaw fit, Glossopteris, tillites, placer gold Ghana–Brazil; forces: pole-fleeing & tidal — inadequate), Arthur Holmes (convection currents 1930s), Harry Hess sea-floor spreading 1961 (palaeomagnetic stripes — Vine & Matthews), Morgan/McKenzie plate tectonics 1967–68.
  • Seven majors (Pacific largest, Antarctic, N. American, S. American, Eurasian, African, Indo-Australian) + minors (Nazca, Cocos, Arabian, Philippine, Caribbean, Juan de Fuca, Scotia). Boundaries: divergent (mid-Atlantic ridge, East African Rift, Red Sea), convergent (ocean–continent Andes; ocean–ocean Japan/Marianas/Andaman arc; continent–continent Himalaya), transform (San Andreas). Hotspots (Hawaii, Réunion → Deccan). Indian plate moved ~15–20 cm/yr; collision ~50 Ma; still 5 cm/yr NE.

Rocks & minerals

  • Igneous (primary; intrusive/plutonic — granite, gabbro; extrusive — basalt, rhyolite, obsidian, pumice), Sedimentary (stratified; clastic — sandstone, shale, conglomerate; chemical — limestone, rock salt; organic — coal; fossils; 75% surface, 5% crust volume), Metamorphic (heat/pressure — contact/thermal & regional/dynamic; foliated: slate←shale, schist, gneiss←granite; non-foliated: marble←limestone, quartzite←sandstone, anthracite←coal). Rock cycle. Mohs scale (talc 1 → diamond 10). Bowen's reaction series.

Landforms by agent (define-by-feature bank)

  • Weathering (in situ: physical — frost, exfoliation/onion, salt; chemical — carbonation (karst), hydration, oxidation, solution; biological) vs mass movement (creep, solifluction, slump, landslide, debris flow) vs erosion (transport). Exogenic vs endogenic; geomorphic cycle (Davis: youth–maturity–old; Penck).
  • Fluvial: V-valley, gorge (hard rock; Indus), canyon (horizontal strata, arid; Grand Canyon), waterfalls (Jog, Angel), potholes, plunge pools, meanders, oxbow lakes, floodplains, natural levees, point bars, braided channels, river terraces, alluvial fans (piedmont), deltas (arcuate — Nile, Ganga; bird's-foot — Mississippi; cuspate — Tiber; estuarine — Narmada/Tapi), peneplain, monadnock/inselberg (residual), river capture/piracy, knick point, incised/entrenched meanders.
  • Glacial: cirque/corrie (armchair) → tarn lake; arête, horn (Matterhorn), U-shaped valley, hanging valley (waterfalls), fjord (drowned U-valley — Norway), roche moutonnée, crag & tail; depositional — moraines (lateral, medial, terminal, ground), drumlins (basket of eggs; blunt end up-ice), eskers (sinuous, sub-glacial streams), kames, kettle holes, outwash plains, erratics, till/boulder clay, varves.
  • Aeolian/arid: deflation hollows (Qattara), yardangs (parallel ridges), zeugen (table), mushroom/pedestal rocks, ventifacts, desert pavement/reg, inselbergs, pediments, playas (salt lakes; Sambhar), bajada, mesa → butte, wadi; dunes — barchan (crescent, horns downwind), seif/longitudinal, transverse, parabolic (vegetated; horns upwind), star; loess (wind-blown silt — China, Hwang Ho).
  • Karst (limestone; carbonation): sinkholes/dolines (solution, collapse), uvala, polje, swallow holes, lapies/karren, caves — stalactites (ceiling), stalagmites (floor), columns, blind valleys, cockpit karst, tower karst (Guilin); India — Borra (AP), Belum (AP), Meghalaya (Mawsmai, Krem Liat Prah longest), Kutumsar (Chhattisgarh), Robber's cave.
  • Coastal: cliffs, wave-cut platforms, sea caves → arches → stacks → stumps, blowholes/geos, spits (Chilika), bars, tombolo (connects island), lagoons (Chilika, Pulicat, Vembanad), beaches, barrier islands, cuspate foreland, raised beaches (emergent), rias, fjords, dalmatian (submergent); coral reefs — fringing, barrier (Great Barrier), atoll (Lakshadweep; Darwin subsidence theory); mangroves.
  • Groundwater: aquifer, aquiclude, artesian well, water table, springs, geysers (Old Faithful), hot springs (Manikaran, Tattapani).

Mountains & structural forms

  • Fold (young: Himalaya, Alps, Andes, Rockies — Alpine orogeny; old: Aravalli (world's oldest fold), Urals, Appalachians), block/horst (Vosges, Black Forest; Satpura?) & rift/graben (Rhine, Narmada-Tapi, East Africa, Baikal, Dead Sea), volcanic (Kilimanjaro, Fuji), residual/relict (Nilgiri, Parasnath). Fold terms — anticline, syncline, recumbent, overthrust/nappe; fault types — normal, reverse/thrust, strike-slip; plateau types — intermontane (Tibet, Bolivia), piedmont (Patagonia), continental (Deccan), lava (Columbia, Deccan), dissected (Chota Nagpur). Plains — structural, erosional (peneplain), depositional (alluvial, glacial, loess, lacustrine — Kashmir karewas).

Traps

  • Barchan horns point downwind; parabolic horns upwind.
  • Drumlin's blunt end faces the ice-source; stalactites hang down ("c" for ceiling).
  • Fjord = glacial + submergence; ria = drowned river valley.
  • S-waves don't cross the outer core — evidence it is liquid.

Key Points & Mindmap

Skeleton facts and recall triggers.

Concept-anchor flash.

Interior flash

  • Conrad → within crust · Moho → crust-mantle · Gutenberg → mantle-core · Lehmann → inner core.
  • S-wave shadow → liquid outer core · isostasy → Airy (roots) vs Pratt (density).

Plate flash

  • Wegener 1912 drift · Hess 1961 sea-floor spreading · 7 major plates, Indian ~5-6 cm/yr NE.
  • Convergent trio → Andes (o-c), Japan (o-o), Himalaya (c-c) · divergent → mid-Atlantic ridge · transform → San Andreas.
  • Hotspots → Hawaii intra-plate; Reunion → Deccan Traps.

Quake-volcano flash

  • Richter = magnitude (energy) · Mercalli = intensity (damage) · P-waves fastest, solids+liquids.
  • India zones II-V · zone V → Himalaya-NE-Kutch-Andaman · Barren Island only active.
  • Intrusive set → batholith-laccolith-lopolith-phacolith-sill-dyke.

Landform flash

  • Fluvial → V-gorge-waterfall (young), meander-oxbow (mature), delta-peneplain (old).
  • Arid → yardang-zeugen-inselberg-playa · loess wind-blown · glacial → cirque-horn-moraine-esker-fjord.
  • Coastal → spit-bar-lagoon-cliff · Karst → sinkhole-stalactite-cave.

Trap flash

  • Delta types: bird-foot = Mississippi; arcuate = Nile; estuarine = Narmada-Tapi.
  • Fjord = glacial erosion, later sea-filled (Norway) — not fluvial.
  • Deccan Traps = flood basalt (fissure eruption), not cone volcano.
  • Bihar = seismic zone IV (not V) — zone-V list trap.

Q1. The fact that S-waves do not travel through the outer core indicates that it is: (a) Very dense solid (b) Liquid (c) Made of iron only (d) At very low pressure

Q2. Match the landform with the agent: A. Drumlin — 1. Wind · B. Barchan — 2. Glacier · C. Stalagmite — 3. Groundwater (a) A-2 B-1 C-3 (b) A-1 B-2 C-3 (c) A-3 B-1 C-2 (d) A-2 B-3 C-1

Q3. Consider: 1. Sedimentary rocks cover about three-fourths of the earth's land surface but form a small fraction of crustal volume. 2. Marble is a metamorphosed form of sandstone. 3. Gneiss is a foliated metamorphic rock. (a) 1 and 2 (b) 1 and 3 (c) 2 and 3 (d) 1, 2 and 3

QAnsWhy

Part I — GS Paper I — General Studies (Prelims) · Chapter 2: Geography

Lesson 1.2.2

Climatology: Atmosphere, Cyclones & Monsoon

In this lessonDetailed StudyRevision DigestKey Points & MindmapDiagrams, Maps & FlowchartsPrevious Year Questions

Detailed Study

The full treatment of this lesson.

Atmosphere layers, circulation, cyclones, Koppen-in-India, and monsoon mechanics — the prelims workhorse.

1. Atmosphere structure

  • Layers: troposphere (0-12 km, weather, lapse ~6.5C/km) → tropopause → stratosphere (calm; ozone layer 15-35 km; jets sit near its base) → mesosphere (meteors burn) → thermosphere-ionosphere (aurora, radio) → exosphere.
  • Insolation budget: albedo ~30%, absorbed ~70%; heat transfer (conduction-convection-advection); temperature inversion types (radiation — valley fog, frontal, subsidence, advection). Greenhouse effect basics; aerosols-CCN role in cloud physics.

2. Pressure belts & winds

  • Belts: equatorial low (ITCZ, doldrums), subtropical highs (horse latitudes ~30), subpolar lows, polar highs; seasonal migration follows the sun (ITCZ shifts over India in monsoon). Winds: planetary (trades NE/SE, westerlies, polar easterlies), periodic (monsoon, land-sea breeze, mountain-valley), local (loo, kalbaisakhi, mango showers, mistral, bora, chinook, foehn, sirocco, harmattan).
  • Jet streams: subtropical westerly jet (winter, drives western disturbances), tropical easterly jet (summer, near 15N, upper-air monsoon aid); Rossby waves.

3. Cyclones & precipitation

  • Tropical cyclones: warm-core, no fronts, eye-eye-wall; form 5-20 lat (Coriolis minimum at equator); conditions: SST >27C, low shear, pre-existing disturbance, upper divergence; seasonal peaks (pre/post-monsoon Bay of Bengal dominance); IMD naming list (13 countries, 2020 revision). Temperate cyclones: front-based (warm-cold-occluded), west-to-east, winter western disturbances → NW India rain-snow.
  • Precipitation forms: convectional (4pm equatorial), orographic (Cherrapunji-Mawsynram relief trap), frontal/cyclonic; humidity terms (RH, dew point); fog types (radiation, advection).

4. Koppen-in-India & monsoon

  • India Koppen: Am (Malabar coast), Aw (most of peninsula-interior), BWhw/BShw (NW interior, rain shadows), Cwg (Gangetic plain), Cwb (NE hills-shillong), Dfc (Arunachal high altitude), E (Ladakh).
  • Monsoon mechanics: differential heating + ITCZ shift + Tibetan plateau heating + jet-stream reversal + Somali current + Indian Ocean Dipole; onset Kerala ~1 Jun (±1 week), MOK withdrawal Oct; breaks-monsoon lows; ENSO-IOD-MJO modulators; monsoon sub-divisions (IMD 36).

MCQ hooks

  • Ozone in stratosphere (not mesosphere); lapse 6.5C/km normal.
  • Subtropical jet = winter western disturbances; tropical easterly jet = summer monsoon helper.
  • Tropical cyclone formation minimum ~5 lat (Coriolis zero at equator).
  • Koppen codes in India: Am-Malabar, Aw-peninsula, Cwg-plain, Dfc-NE, E-Ladakh.
  • Western disturbances = winter NW India rain (rabi aid).
  • Chinook-foehn = warm descent winds; mistral = cold north wind (France).

Revision Digest

Condensed for the last mile before the exam.

Prelims GS-I › Geography › Physical Geography. Mechanism questions (why/where) dominate; keep the diagrams in your head.

Atmosphere

  • Composition: N₂ 78.08%, O₂ 20.95%, Ar 0.93%, CO₂ ~0.04% (≈420 ppm 2024); water vapour 0–4%; ozone (10–50 km, peak ~25 km; Dobson unit). Layers: troposphere (8 km poles–18 km equator; lapse rate 6.5 °C/km; all weather; tropopause) → stratosphere (ozone; temperature rises; jets fly) → mesosphere (coldest −90 °C; meteors burn) → thermosphere/ionosphere (aurora, radio reflection; ISS ~400 km) → exosphere. Homosphere/heterosphere split at 80 km.
  • Insolation & heat budget: ~1.94 cal/cm²/min solar constant; albedo ~30–35% (planetary); 51% absorbed by surface; greenhouse (H₂O, CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, O₃, CFCs); terrestrial radiation long-wave; latitudinal heat balance → winds/currents; aphelion 4 July, perihelion 3 Jan; temperature controls — latitude, altitude, continentality, currents, winds, slope; inversion (radiation/valley — frost; subsidence; frontal; advection); normal vs environmental lapse rate; adiabatic — DALR 10 °C/km, SALR ~6 °C/km; stability.
  • Pressure belts: equatorial low (doldrums/ITCZ), sub-tropical highs (30°; horse latitudes), sub-polar lows (60°), polar highs; shift with sun. Winds: Coriolis (zero at equator, max at poles; right in NH — Ferrel's law; geostrophic wind), pressure-gradient, friction. Planetary — trades (NE/SE), westerlies (roaring 40s, furious 50s, shrieking 60s), polar easterlies; tri-cellular model (Hadley, Ferrel, Polar); jet streams (STJ ~30° N, 12 km; polar front jet; Tropical Easterly Jet in summer over India; Somali jet low-level); Rossby waves; walker circulation.
  • Local winds: Foehn (Alps), Chinook (Rockies; snow-eater), Mistral (cold; Rhône), Bora (Adriatic), Sirocco (Sahara→Med), Harmattan (W Africa; "doctor"), Khamsin (Egypt), Loo (India), Santa Ana (California), Zonda (Andes), Brickfielder (Australia), Pampero (Argentina), Norwester/Kalbaisakhi (Bengal), Mango showers (Kerala/Karnataka), Cherry blossom (Karnataka), Blizzard, Buran, Purga, Levanter, Berg (S Africa), Bise, Tramontane, Elephanta (Malabar Sept–Oct), Nor'westers, land/sea & mountain/valley (anabatic/katabatic) breezes.
  • Humidity: absolute, specific, relative (temperature-dependent), dew point; condensation forms — dew, frost, fog (radiation, advection, frontal, upslope), mist, smog, clouds — high (cirrus, cirrostratus (halo), cirrocumulus; 6–12 km), middle (altostratus, altocumulus), low (stratus, nimbostratus, stratocumulus), vertical (cumulus, cumulonimbus — thunderstorms/hail). Precipitation types: convectional (equatorial 4 pm), orographic (windward; rain shadow — Pune, Patagonia), cyclonic/frontal; forms — rain, snow, sleet, hail, drizzle; virga.
  • Air masses (cP, mP, cT, mT, cA) & fronts (warm — stratiform, gradual; cold — cumulonimbus, squall; occluded; stationary). Temperate/extra-tropical cyclones (polar front theory — Bjerknes; 1,000–2,000 km; move W→E with westerlies; winter; western disturbances over India from Mediterranean — rabi rain, Himalayan snow).

Tropical cyclones

  • Conditions: SST >26.5–27 °C to 50–60 m depth, Coriolis (form beyond 5° latitude), low vertical wind shear, pre-existing low-level disturbance, upper-level divergence, humid mid-troposphere. Structure — eye (calm, subsiding, 30–50 km), eye-wall (max wind), spiral rain bands; moves with easterlies then recurves; weakens over land (no moisture, friction). Names: hurricane (Atlantic/E Pacific), typhoon (NW Pacific — most), cyclone (Indian Ocean), willy-willy (Australia), baguio (Philippines); Saffir–Simpson 1–5 (≥119 km/h); IMD scale: Depression (31–49) → Deep depression → Cyclonic storm 62–88 → Severe 89–117 → Very severe 118–165 → Extremely severe 166–220 → Super cyclone >221 km/h. Bay of Bengal 4:1 Arabian Sea (warmer, shallower, more disturbances from Pacific; now Arabian Sea rising — Tauktae, Biparjoy). Peaks: Oct–Nov & May. Naming — WMO/ESCAP panel 13 countries (list 2020: 169 names; Amphan last of old list; Nisarga first new). Recent: Fani 2019, Amphan 2020, Tauktae/Yaas 2021, Asani/Sitrang/Mandous 2022, Biparjoy/Michaung 2023, Remal, Dana, Fengal 2024, Shakhti/Montha 2025. Storm surge = biggest killer (1999 Odisha 10,000). Tornado — mesocyclone, Fujita scale (EF0–5), US Tornado Alley; waterspouts.

Monsoon (India)

  • Classical: differential heating (Halley), ITCZ shift (Flohn), Tibetan plateau heating (anticyclone → TEJ), subtropical westerly jet shifting north of Himalaya (~ June 1 Kerala onset), Somali low-level jet, Mascarene high (SE trades cross equator → SW), ENSO/IOD/MJO modulation. Branches: Arabian Sea (Western Ghats windward; Mumbai ~ June 10; rain shadow Deccan; Aravalli parallel → Rajasthan dry) & Bay of Bengal (Meghalaya — Mawsynram/Cherrapunji funnel; deflected west by Himalaya → Ganga plain; Delhi ~ late June; Kalbaisakhi earlier). Break monsoon (trough shifts to Himalayan foothills → NE & foothills rain, plains dry). Onset over Kerala normal 1 June; covers India 8 July (revised normal dates 2020); withdrawal from NW 17 Sept (starts), from India by 15 Oct; retreating/NE monsoon Oct–Dec — TN, coastal AP, Rayalaseema, S Karnataka, Kerala (~48% TN's rain); Long Period Average 87 cm (1971–2020); normal 96–104% LPA.
  • ENSO: El Niño (warm E Pacific; weak Walker; Indian drought tendency — 2023 El Niño, 2024 La Niña-neutral), La Niña (cold; good monsoon; floods); ENSO Modoki; IOD (Saji 1999; positive = warm W Indian Ocean, good for monsoon; DMI); MJO (30–60 days eastward; active phase over Indian Ocean boosts rain); Atlantic Niño; Eurasian snow cover (negative). IMD forecasts April & May (MMCFS + dynamic; ensemble). Kharif sowing link.
  • Seasons (IMD): winter Jan–Feb (western disturbances; Jan coldest; NE trades), pre-monsoon/hot Mar–May (Loo, Kalbaisakhi, mango showers, cherry blossom; heat low over Thar; May hottest NW), SW monsoon Jun–Sep, post-monsoon/retreating Oct–Dec (Oct heat; cyclones).
  • Climatic regions: Köppen — India: Amw (W coast), As (Coromandel), Aw (peninsula), BShw (Rajasthan-Gujarat), BWhw (Thar), Cwg (Ganga plain), Dfc (Arunachal), E/ET (Himalaya); Thornthwaite; Trewartha; Stamp; Koeppen letters — A tropical, B dry, C warm temperate, D cold, E polar; f no dry season, m monsoon, w winter dry, s summer dry.

Traps

  • Coriolis is zero at the equator — cyclones form beyond ±5°.
  • Cyclone eye = subsiding air, calm; eyewall = strongest winds.
  • El Niño → weak Indian monsoon (tendency, not rule — 1997 was normal).
  • Positive IOD helps monsoon; can offset El Niño (2019).
  • Cherrapunji vs Mawsynram: Mawsynram wettest; both Khasi hills, Bay branch.
  • Extra-tropical cyclones have fronts; tropical don't.

Anchor flash.

Layer flash

  • Troposphere → weather, 6.5C/km lapse · stratosphere → ozone (15-35 km) · mesosphere → meteors · thermosphere → aurora-ionosphere.
  • Albedo ~30% · inversion types → radiation (valley), frontal, subsidence, advection.

Wind flash

  • ITCZ → doldrums, migrates with sun · horse latitudes ~30 · westerlies 30-60.
  • Subtropical westerly jet → winter, western disturbances · tropical easterly jet → summer monsoon.
  • Local winds → loo (N India heat), kalbaisakhi (Bengal thunder), mango showers (Kerala), chinook-foehn (warm), mistral-bora (cold), sirocco (Sahara→Europe), harmattan (W Africa dust).

Cyclone flash

  • Tropical → warm core, eye, 5-20 lat, SST>27C, IMD 13-country naming · Bay of Bengal dominance.
  • Temperate → fronts (warm-cold-occluded), winter western disturbances → rabi rain-snow.

Koppen flash

  • Am → Malabar · Aw → peninsula · BShw → NW interior · Cwg → Gangetic plain · Cwb → Shillong-NE hills · Dfc → Arunachal · E → Ladakh.

Monsoon flash

  • Drivers → ITCZ shift + Tibetan heating + jet reversal + Somali current + ENSO-IOD-MJO · onset Kerala 1 Jun ±1 week · monsoon trough breaks → dry spells.

Trap flash

  • Equator = no cyclone genesis (Coriolis ~0) — 5-degree rule.
  • Mawsynram > Cherrapunji in annual rainfall — order trap.
  • Ozone hole = Antarctic spring — not Arctic-first.
  • Jet streams live near tropopause — not mid-stratosphere.

Part I — GS Paper I — General Studies (Prelims) · Chapter 2: Geography

Lesson 1.2.3

Oceanography: Currents, Tides & Salinity

In this lessonDetailed StudyRevision DigestKey Points & MindmapDiagrams, Maps & FlowchartsPrevious Year Questions

Detailed Study

The full treatment of this lesson.

Ocean relief, salinity-temperature, currents, ENSO-IOD, tides-mangroves-resources. Statement-match territory.

1. Relief, salinity, temperature

  • Relief: continental shelf (richest fishing-oil; India ~west coast wider), slope, rise, abyssal plain, trenches (Mariana ~11 km deepest; Java trench near India); mid-ocean ridges; seamounts-guyots.
  • Salinity: mean 35 ppt; max belts = subtropical highs (~20-30 lat) due to evaporation>precipitation; Red Sea ~41 ppt (highest), Dead Sea lake ~330; Baltic-lowest oceans-side (freshwater dilution); equator-lower (rain).
  • Temperature: surface warm belts; annual range small (water heat capacity); thermocline layer; cold currents flow along the west coasts of continents (Benguela, Canary, California, Peru).

2. Currents & oscillations

  • Drivers: wind (trade push), Coriolis (gyres — clockwise N, anticlockwise S), density-thermohaline (NADW conveyor). Famous: Gulf Stream + North Atlantic Drift (warms NW Europe), Kuroshio (warm, Japan), Oyashio (cold, meets → fog-fisheries Japan), Labrador (icebergs Grand Banks), Peru/Humboldt (cold, upwelling, guano), Benguela-Canary-California cold, Agulhas-Mozambique warm (Indian Ocean), monsoon drift reversal (N Indian Ocean unique seasonal reversal).
  • El Nino: eastern-equatorial Pacific warming; Walker circulation collapses; Peru floods-fisheries crash (anchoveta), Australian-Indian drought tendency; La Nina opposite (good monsoon bias). IOD: west-minus-east Indian Ocean SST dipole (positive = good monsoon); MJO: 30-60-day eastward pulse; triple-dip La Nina 2020-22 era anchor.

3. Tides, coasts, resources

  • Tides: spring (sun-moon aligned, full-new moon, high range), neap (90 degrees, low range); perigean-spring extreme; tidal energy pilots (Gulf of Kutch, Gulf of Khambhat studies); Gulf of Cambay highest tidal range India.
  • Coastal: mangroves (Sundarbans largest; Bhitarkanika second), coral reefs (fringing-barrier-atoll; Gulf of Mannar-Palk Bay, Gulf of Kutch, Andaman-Nicobar, Lakshadweep atolls), coral bleaching = SST stress (El Nino years).
  • Resources: polymetallic nodules (Mn-Ni-Co-Cu; Clarion-Clipperton Zone; India's reserved area in Central Indian Ocean Basin via ISA), gas hydrates, offshore oil (Mumbai High), salt pans (Gujarat), Blue Economy + Deep Ocean Mission (2021, Samudrayaan MATSYA-6000), PMMSY fisheries, Sagarmala ports.

MCQ hooks

  • Red Sea highest ocean-side salinity; Baltic lowest; Dead Sea = lake (not ocean).
  • Gulf Stream-NAD warms Europe; Peru cold current + El Nino interplay.
  • Spring vs neap tide alignment rule; Kutch-Khambhat high ranges.
  • Nodules: Mn-Ni-Co-Cu; India's CIOB claim via International Seabed Authority.
  • IOD positive = good monsoon; MJO = 30-60-day oscillation.
  • Lakshadweep = atolls; Andaman = volcanic arc (Barren Island).

Revision Digest

Condensed for the last mile before the exam.

Prelims GS-I › Geography › Physical Geography. Current–coast matching, salinity anomalies, and tide mechanics.

Relief & basics

  • Oceans ~71% (361 million km²); Pacific (largest, deepest — Mariana Trench/Challenger Deep ~10,994 m), Atlantic (S-shaped; Puerto Rico trench), Indian (Java/Sunda trench), Southern (60° S; 2000), Arctic (smallest, shallowest). Relief: continental shelf (avg 80 km; 150–200 m; 7.5%; fishing/oil — Siberian widest), continental slope (2–5°; shelf break; submarine canyons), continental rise, abyssal plain (40%), mid-ocean ridges (Mid-Atlantic; 65,000 km system), trenches (subduction), seamounts/guyots (flat-topped), atolls, submarine canyons (Congo), banks (Dogger, Grand Banks), Sea knolls. Sediments: terrigenous (mud), biogenic oozes (calcareous — Globigerina, pteropod (<4,000 m; CCD); siliceous — diatom (cold), radiolarian (tropical)), red clay (deep Pacific; hydrogenous), manganese nodules (Clarion-Clipperton; India's PMN area Central Indian Ocean Basin; Deep Ocean Mission — Samudrayaan/Matsya-6000).
  • UNCLOS 1982 (India 1995): baseline → territorial sea 12 nm → contiguous zone 24 nm → EEZ 200 nm → continental shelf up to 350 nm (India's extended claim); high seas; ISA (Jamaica; Area); ITLOS (Hamburg); BBNJ/High Seas Treaty 2023 (India signed Sept 2024; ratifications → enters into force Jan 2026).

Temperature & salinity

  • Surface temperature avg 27 °C at equator → decreases poleward; thermocline (200–1,000 m; rapid fall); three-layer; NH warmer than SH; max ~20° N not equator (cloud); daily range 1 °C, annual 5 °C (10 °C tropics). Enclosed seas warmer.
  • Salinity avg 35‰; controls — evaporation, precipitation, river inflow, freezing/melting, currents; highest in sub-tropics (~37‰), low equator (rain), lowest near poles & river mouths (Bay of Bengal 30–33 vs Arabian Sea 36–37). Extremes: Lake Van 330‰, Dead Sea 240‰, Great Salt Lake 220‰, Red Sea 41‰ (highest open sea), Mediterranean 39‰, Baltic 7‰ (lowest sea), Black Sea 18‰. Halocline; sea ice brine rejection; salinity increases density → thermohaline circulation (Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation — AMOC; slowdown risk; NADW, AABW).

Currents (gyres clockwise NH, anticlockwise SH — Coriolis; western boundary currents warm, fast, narrow)

OceanWarmCold
N AtlanticGulf Stream → N Atlantic Drift (NW Europe mild), N Equatorial, Antilles, Florida, Norwegian, IrmingerLabrador (Grand Banks fog + fish), Canary, East Greenland
S AtlanticBrazil, S EquatorialBenguela (Namib), Falkland
N PacificKuroshio (Japan), N Pacific Drift, Alaska, N Equatorial, TsushimaOyashio/Kurile, California
S PacificEast Australian, S EquatorialHumboldt/Peru (Atacama; anchovy; El Niño disrupts), West Australian
IndianAgulhas, Mozambique, monsoon drift (reverses — SW summer, NE winter), S EquatorialWest Australian, Somali (cold upwelling in SW monsoon!)
Southern—West Wind Drift/Antarctic Circumpolar (largest)
  • Effects: fishing grounds at warm–cold meeting (Grand Banks, NW Pacific, Newfoundland); fog; coastal deserts on cold-current west coasts (Atacama, Namib, Kalahari, Sonora, W Australia); mild winters (Norway ice-free ports); upwelling zones (Peru, California, Benguela, Canary, Somali) — nutrient-rich; Sargasso Sea (gyre centre, boundary-less); Ekman spiral/transport (45° right of wind); "garbage patches".

Tides

  • Moon (2.17× sun's effect); spring tides (syzygy — new & full moon; 2×/month), neap (quadrature — 1st/3rd quarter); perigean (moon closest; biggest), apogean; semi-diurnal (2 highs/day; 12 h 25 min apart — Atlantic), diurnal (Gulf of Mexico), mixed (Pacific); tidal bore (Hooghly, Qiantang), tidal range max Bay of Fundy 15–16 m, India — Gulf of Khambhat (11 m) & Kutch (8 m); Sundarbans; tidal energy projects. Ebb/flood; equilibrium (Newton) vs dynamic (Laplace, amphidromic points) theory. Tsunamis are not tides (seismic; 800 km/h deep ocean; INCOIS warning centre Hyderabad; 2004 Dec 26).

Coral & marine ecology hooks

  • Corals: 20–30 °C, <50 m, clear saline shallow, zooxanthellae symbiosis; bleaching (2024 fourth global event); reef types fringing (Andaman, Gulf of Kutch), barrier (GBR; Gulf of Mannar patches), atoll (Lakshadweep, Maldives); India reefs — Gulf of Mannar, Gulf of Kutch, Lakshadweep, Andaman-Nicobar, Malvan, Netrani; Coral Triangle; ocean acidification (pH 8.1 → 8.0; aragonite); dead zones/hypoxia (Gulf of Mexico; Arabian Sea OMZ largest); marine heatwaves; sea-level rise ~3.7 mm/yr (thermal expansion + ice); Indian Ocean warming fastest; blue carbon (mangroves, seagrass — Palk Bay dugong reserve 2022, salt marsh); Sargassum; Mission Sagar, SAGAR, MAHASAGAR (2025); Blue Economy policy; ONGC deep-water KG-D5.

Traps

  • Highest salinity is in the sub-tropics, not the equator; Red Sea > Mediterranean > Persian Gulf among seas; Lake Van > Dead Sea among lakes.
  • Somali current is cold during the SW monsoon (upwelling) though in a tropical ocean.
  • Spring tide ≠ spring season; occurs twice a month.
  • Labrador (cold) meets Gulf Stream (warm) → Grand Banks; Oyashio meets Kuroshio → Japan fishing.

Key Points & Mindmap

Skeleton facts and recall triggers.

Current-and-fact flash.

Salinity flash

  • Mean 35 ppt · max belt 20-30 lat · Red Sea ~41 highest · Baltic lowest · equator lower (rain dilution).

Current flash

  • Warm → Gulf Stream-NAD, Kuroshio, Brazil, Agulhas, East Australian · cold → Peru-Humboldt, Benguela, Canary, California, Oyashio, Labrador, West Australian.
  • N Indian Ocean → unique monsoon drift reversal · gyres → clockwise N hemisphere.
  • Upwelling fisheries → Peru, Benguela, Somali (summer monsoon).

ENSO-IOD flash

  • El Nino → east Pacific warm, weak monsoon bias · La Nina → opposite · IOD positive → good monsoon · MJO → 30-60-day pulse.
  • Walker circulation weakens in El Nino years.

Tide-resource flash

  • Spring tide → full-new moon alignment · neap → quarter 90 degrees · Gulf of Khambhat highest Indian range.
  • Mangroves → Sundarbans largest, Bhitarkanika second · reefs → fringing-barrier-atoll; bleaching = warm SST.
  • Nodules → Mn-Ni-Co-Cu, CIOB/CCZ, ISA regime · Deep Ocean Mission 2021, Samudrayaan.

Trap flash

  • Cold currents on western continental margins — not eastern.
  • Dead Sea = hypersaline lake; Red Sea = highest sea salinity.
  • Mariana Trench = Pacific (not Indian); Java/Sunda = Indian Ocean trench.
  • Neap tide = quarter moons — not full moon.
  • Indian Ocean monsoon current reversal = unique (Atlantic-Pacific gyres permanent).

Previous Year Questions

What the examiner has actually asked.

8 original prelims-pattern questions; key with one-line reasoning at the end.

Q1. Which of the following is a cold current? (a) Kuroshio (b) Agulhas (c) Benguela (d) Brazil

Q2. Consider ocean salinity: 1. It is highest at the equator due to high temperature. 2. The Bay of Bengal is less saline than the Arabian Sea. 3. Lake Van has salinity higher than the Dead Sea. (a) 1 and 2 (b) 2 and 3 (c) 1 and 3 (d) 1, 2 and 3

Part I — GS Paper I — General Studies (Prelims) · Chapter 2: Geography

Lesson 1.2.4

Biogeography: Soils & Natural Vegetation

In this lessonDetailed StudyRevision DigestKey Points & MindmapDiagrams, Maps & FlowchartsPrevious Year Questions

Detailed Study

The full treatment of this lesson.

Biomes, diversity metrics, island theory, soil-vegetation links. Light-read area with trick MCQs.

1. Biomes & vegetation belts

  • Whittaker's frame: temperature x precipitation → biome. Sequence pole-to-equator: tundra → taiga (boreal coniferous) → temperate deciduous-grassland → Mediterranean scrub → desert → tropical rainforest (max NPP) → savanna.
  • India forest types (Champion-Seth 1968, 16 major groups): tropical evergreen (Western Ghats-NE-Andaman), tropical deciduous (most extensive — moist then dry), tropical thorn (NW), montane (oak-conifer above), littoral-swamp (mangroves), alpine. Forest Survey of India (ISFR biennial): forest+tree cover ~25% of geographic area (verify latest ISFR figure).

2. Biodiversity metrics & hotspots

  • Metrics: alpha (within habitat), beta (between-habitat change), gamma (landscape total). Endemism: species confined to an area (India: high in Himalaya-Western Ghats-Andaman). India's 4 hotspots (of 36 global): Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, Sundaland (Nicobars).
  • Species roles: keystone (ecosystem-defining: tigers, sea otters), flagship (iconic: panda), umbrella, indicator; IUCN categories: EX-EW-CR-EN-VU-NT-LC-DD-NE; Red List updates annual.
  • Island biogeography (MacArthur-Wilson 1967): species richness rises with area, falls with isolation; immigration-extinction balance; SIBA-conservation design basis.

3. Soil-vegetation geography

  • Soil classification (ICAR 8-fold): alluvial (largest; khadar-new vs bangar-old), black/regur (cotton; Deccan basalt, moisture-retentive, self-ploughing), red (ferruginous, weathered crystalline), laterite (intense leaching; brick-tea-cashew), arid (calcified; kankar layers), saline-usara (alkaline; irrigation mismanagement), peaty-organic (Kerala), forest-mountain soils.
  • Soil-vegetation coupling: laterite ↔ degraded deciduous; black ↔ dry savanna-ish zones; alluvium ↔ agriculture belt; erosion (sheet-rill-gully-ravine — Chambal badlands) + conservation (contour bunding, watershed, agroforestry).

MCQ hooks

  • India's 4 hotspots; Andaman-Nicobar chain sits under the Sundaland hotspot.
  • Champion-Seth classification 1968; tropical deciduous = most extensive type.
  • Alpha-beta-gamma definitions verbatim.
  • Black soil = regur = Deccan basalt; laterite = leaching (not lava).
  • Khadar = newer alluvium (flood-refreshed) vs bangar older.
  • MacArthur-Wilson = island theory (area up, richness up).

Revision Digest

Condensed for the last mile before the exam.

Prelims GS-I › Geography › Physical Geography. Soil-type traits (ICAR classification) and biome–climate matching.

Soil formation & profile

  • Factors (Jenny): parent material, climate, relief, organisms, time (Cl-O-R-P-T). Processes: weathering → humification → eluviation/illuviation, laterisation (hot-wet; silica leached, Fe/Al oxides stay), podzolisation (cool-wet coniferous; acidic, ash-grey), calcification (semi-arid; CaCO₃), salinisation/alkalisation (arid; capillary rise), gleisation (waterlogged). Profile: O (organic) → A (topsoil, humus; eluviation) → E → B (illuviation; subsoil) → C (regolith) → R (bedrock). Texture triangle (sand-silt-clay; loam best); pH (6.5–7.5 ideal); soil health card (12 parameters — NPK, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, pH, EC, OC); NBSS&LUP (Nagpur).

Indian soils (ICAR 8 major)

India's vegetation (Champion & Seth 1968 — 16 types; ISFR 2023: forest cover 7,15,343 km² = 21.76%, tree cover 3.41%, total 25.17%; MP largest area, Mizoram highest %; Lakshadweep ~90%; mangroves 4,992 km² — WB 42%)

  • Tropical evergreen (>200 cm; W Ghats, NE, A&N; rosewood, ebony, mahogany, aini), semi-evergreen; tropical moist deciduous (100–200 cm; most widespread; teak, sal, shisham, sandalwood; Chhota Nagpur, Ghats foothills); tropical dry deciduous (70–100 cm; teak, tendu, palas, khair; UP, MP, peninsular interior); thorn/scrub (<70 cm; acacia, babul, khejri, ber, date; Rajasthan, Gujarat, Deccan rain shadow); montane (wet temperate — Nilgiri sholas; Himalayan — oak, chestnut, pine, deodar, silver fir, spruce, birch; alpine — juniper, rhododendron); littoral/mangrove (Sundarbans — Heritiera fomes (sundari), Rhizophora, Avicennia; Bhitarkanika, Pichavaram, Godavari-Krishna, Gulf of Kutch; pneumatophores, viviparity). Forest Survey of India (Dehradun; biennial ISFR); National Forest Policy 1988 (33% target); Van Mahotsav (July); Green India Mission; CAMPA; Nagar Van; Mangrove — MISHTI 2023; Great Indian Bustard grasslands; sacred groves (Meghalaya law kyntang, Kerala kavu, Rajasthan oran, Karnataka devarakadu).

Traps

  • Black soil is rich in Ca, Mg, K, Fe but poor in N, P, humus — same NPH deficiency as most Indian soils.
  • Laterite forms under alternating wet-dry tropical conditions, and hardens like brick (Latin later).
  • Khadar = new & fertile; bhangar = old & kankar-rich (not the reverse).
  • Chernozem = temperate grasslands; latosol = rainforest; podzol = taiga.
  • ISFR 2023 (released Dec 2024): forest+tree cover 25.17%; forest cover alone 21.76%.

Key Points & Mindmap

Skeleton facts and recall triggers.

Term-anchor flash.

Biome flash

  • Max NPP → tropical rainforest · taiga = boreal conifer · savanna = grass+scattered trees · Mediterranean = winter-rain scrub.
  • India forests → Champion-Seth 1968; tropical deciduous largest; mangrove = littoral-swamp type.

Diversity flash

  • Alpha → within-habitat · beta → between-habitat · gamma → landscape total.
  • Hotspots (36 global) → India 4: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, W-Ghats-Sri Lanka, Sundaland.
  • IUCN order → EX, EW, CR, EN, VU, NT, LC (+DD, NE).
  • Keystone → ecosystem-defining · flagship → charismatic · indicator → health signal.

Island flash

  • MacArthur-Wilson 1967 → richness ↑ with area, ↓ with isolation · SIBA application in reserve design.

Soil flash

  • Alluvial largest (khadar new / bangar old) · black = regur, cotton, basalt, self-ploughing · red = crystalline weathering.
  • Laterite → leaching, brick-cashew-tea · arid → kankar · saline-usara → irrigation mismanagement · peaty → Kerala.
  • Ravines → Chambal badlands; gully erosion severe.

Trap flash

  • Laterite ≠ volcanic origin (it's a leaching product).
  • Gamma diversity ≠ 'global' — it's landscape scale.
  • Hotspot criteria: endemic plants ≥1500 + habitat loss ≥70%.
  • Black soil self-ploughing = crack-swell on wetting-drying — not tillage.

Part I — GS Paper I — General Studies (Prelims) · Chapter 2: Geography

Lesson 1.2.5

Physiography: Himalayas, Peninsular Plateau, Plains & Coasts

In this lessonDetailed StudyRevision DigestKey Points & MindmapDiagrams, Maps & FlowchartsPrevious Year Questions

Detailed Study

The full treatment of this lesson.

Five divisions: Himalaya, Northern Plains, Peninsula, Coasts-Islands, Desert. Passes, doabs, gaps — direct ask zone.

1. The Himalaya

  • North-to-south: Trans-Himalaya (Karakoram-Ladakh-Zanskar; K2 Godwin-Austen) → Great Himalaya (Himadri; Everest-Sagarmatha; Kanchenjunga = India's highest) → Lesser/Middle (Himachal; Dhauladhar-Pir Panjal-Mussoorie-Nag Tibba) → Siwalik/Duns (outer; Bhabar belt below).
  • Regional: Punjab Himalaya (Indus-Sutlej), Kumaon (Sutlej-Kali), Nepal (Kali-Teesta), Assam (Teesta-Dihang). Syntaxial bends: Nanga Parbat (west), Namcha Barwa/Dihang (east). Origin: Tethys closure, India-Asia collision (~50-40 Ma), phased uplift.
  • Major passes: Zoji la-Banihal (J&K), Shipki la (HP-Sutlej entry), Mana-Niti (Uttarakhand), Nathu la-Jelep la (Sikkim), Bomdi la-Diphu (Arunachal).

2. Northern Plains

  • Depositional mega-plain (Indus-Ganga-Brahmaputra); belts: Bhabar (porous gravel; streams vanish) → Terai (marshy re-emergence) → Bhangar (older alluvium, kankar) → Khadar (newer flood-refreshed).
  • Sections: Punjab plain (doabs — Bist-Jalandhar, Bari, Rechna, Chaj, Sind Sagar), Ganga plain (upper-middle-lower; Ganga-Yamuna doab), Brahmaputra valley (Majuli = largest river island).

3. Peninsular plateau

  • Oldest stable block (Archean gneiss); Aravallis (oldest fold range, heavily eroded; Guru Shikhar-Mount Abu), Vindhya-Satpura east-west trend, Maikal-Mahadeo; Deccan Traps (end-Cretaceous flood basalt) under most of Maharashtra.
  • Western Ghats (Sahyadri — continuous, sheer west scarp; Anaimudi highest; gaps: Thal-Bhor, Palghat, Shencottah), Eastern Ghats (discontinuous — Nallamala, Mahendragiri end), Anaimudi 2695 m (Anaimalai), Nilgiri junction (Doddabetta).
  • Plateaus: Malwa (Chambal head), Chotanagpur (minerals; Ranchi), Meghalaya (Garo-Khasi-Jaintia; Shillong peak), Chhattisgarh basin; mineral belts (Chotanagpur-Bastar-Dharwar-Ballari).

4. Coasts, islands, desert

  • West coast: Konkan (Maharashtra-Goa), Kanara (Karnataka), Malabar (Kerala; backwaters-kayals) — narrow, estuaries (Narmada-Tapi), Mumbai High offshore. East coast: Utkal (Odisha), Coromandel (TN-AP) — wide, deltas (Mahanadi-Godavari-Krishna-Kaveri), lagoons (Chilika-Pulicat).
  • Islands: Andaman-Nicobar (~570; Barren-Narcondam volcanoes; Arakan-Yoma arc), Lakshadweep (coral atolls; Minicoy), Gulf of Mannar biosphere.
  • Thar desert: arid-marusthali; longitudinal dunes; barchan (crescent), seif, parabolic; Luni = only major SW-flowing river; Rann (Great-Little) salt flats; Indira Gandhi Canal greened the Sriganganagar belt.

MCQ hooks

  • Order west→east: Karakoram → Great → Lesser → Siwalik (Trans-Himalaya northmost).
  • Passes with states: Zoji la-Banihal (J&K), Shipki la (HP), Nathu-Jelep (Sikkim), Bomdi la (Arunachal).
  • Bhabar-Terai-Bhangar-Khadar sequence moving away from the hills.
  • Anaimudi (2695, Anaimalai) vs Doddabetta (Nilgiri) vs Guru Shikhar (Aravalli).
  • Majuli = Brahmaputra; kayals = Kerala; Chilika = Odisha lagoon.
  • Luni drains SW in Thar; Rann = salt desert (Kutch).

Revision Digest

Condensed for the last mile before the exam.

Prelims GS-I › Geography › Indian Geography. Map-anchored facts: ranges, passes, peaks, hills, coastal plains and islands.

Frame

  • Area 32.87 lakh km² (7th; 2.4% of world land; 17.7% population); lat 8°4′–37°6′ N, long 68°7′–97°25′ E; N–S 3,214 km, E–W 2,933 km; Tropic of Cancer through 8 states (Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, WB, Tripura, Mizoram); IST 82°30′ E (Mirzapur); land frontier 15,200 km (Bangladesh 4,096 longest → China 3,488 → Pakistan 3,323 → Nepal 1,751 → Myanmar 1,643 → Bhutan 699 → Afghanistan 106); coastline 7,516 km (Gujarat longest ~1,600; then Andhra/TN; new 2024 measurement 11,098 km); southernmost point Indira Point (Great Nicobar; 6°45′), mainland Kanyakumari (8°4′); Indira Col northernmost.

Himalayas (young fold; Tethys; ~2,400 km arc, 150–400 km wide; syntaxial bends Nanga Parbat & Namcha Barwa)

  • Trans-Himalaya: Karakoram (K2/Godwin Austen 8,611 — India's highest incl. PoK; Siachen, Baltoro glaciers), Ladakh, Zanskar, Kailash.
  • Greater/Himadri (avg 6,000 m; Everest 8,849 Nepal, Kangchenjunga 8,586 — India's highest, Sikkim; Nanda Devi 7,816 highest wholly in India; Kamet, Nanga Parbat 8,126, Namcha Barwa 7,756).
  • Lesser/Himachal (Pir Panjal — longest; Dhauladhar; Mussoorie; Nag Tibba; Mahabharat (Nepal); hill stations Shimla, Mussoorie, Nainital, Darjeeling; margs Gulmarg/Sonamarg, bugyals; Kashmir & Kangra valleys; karewas — saffron).
  • Outer/Shiwalik (900–1,100 m; duns — Dehradun, Kotli, Patli; Churia in Nepal); bhabar → terai → khadar/bhangar.
  • Regional (Sir Sidney Burrard): Punjab/Kashmir (Indus–Sutlej), Kumaon (Sutlej–Kali; Nanda Devi, Badrinath, Kedarnath, Gangotri), Nepal (Kali–Tista; Everest, Kangchenjunga), Assam (Tista–Dihang; Namcha Barwa). Purvanchal: Patkai Bum, Naga hills (Saramati 3,826), Manipur hills, Mizo/Lushai hills (Blue Mt/Phawngpui), Barail range, Mishmi, Dafla, Abor, Miri; Meghalaya plateau (Garo-Khasi-Jaintia; Shillong peak; part of peninsular block; Mawsynram).
  • Passes: Karakoram (Ladakh–Xinjiang), Khardung La, Zoji La (Srinagar–Leh; Zojila tunnel), Banihal (Jawahar tunnel), Pir Panjal (Mughal road), Rohtang & Atal tunnel (Manali–Lahaul), Baralacha La, Shipki La (Sutlej; HP–Tibet trade), Mana & Niti (Uttarakhand), Lipulekh (Kailash route; India–Nepal–China trijunction), Nathu La & Jelep La (Sikkim–Tibet), Bomdila, Se La (Tawang), Diphu (India–Myanmar–China trijunction), Pangsau (Stilwell Rd), Chang La, Debsa, Bum La, Thang La, Aghil, Lanak La (Aksai Chin), Umling La (highest motorable ~19,024 ft).
  • Glaciers: Siachen (76 km, Karakoram; longest outside polar regions in India), Baltoro, Biafo, Hispar, Batura, Gangotri (30 km; Gaumukh), Zemu (Sikkim), Milam, Pindari, Bara Shigri (HP largest), Drang-Drung; ~9,575 glaciers; Third Pole; GLOF (South Lhonak 2023 Sikkim, Chorabari 2013).

Northern plains (7 lakh km²; 2,400 km; alluvium up to 2,000 m thick)

  • Belts: bhabar (pebbles; streams disappear), terai (marshy, re-emergent), bhangar (old; kankar; barind Bengal, bhur sands), khadar (new). Regional: Punjab-Haryana (doabs — Bist Jalandhar, Bari, Rechna, Chaj, Sindh Sagar; dhaya, bet, chos), Ganga plain (upper/middle/lower; bhur, tal, diara, chaur), Brahmaputra valley (char islands; Majuli), Rajasthan bagar/rohi; Sundarbans delta largest. Ganga–Brahmaputra largest delta.

Peninsular plateau (oldest — Gondwana; Archaean)

  • Central Highlands: Aravalli (oldest fold; Guru Shikhar 1,722 m Mt Abu), Malwa plateau (lava; Chambal ravines), Bundelkhand, Baghelkhand, Vindhya (escarpment; N of Narmada), Satpura (block; Dhupgarh 1,350 highest MP; Amarkantak; Mahadeo, Maikal hills), Chota Nagpur (Ranchi, Hazaribagh, Rajmahal; Parasnath 1,366; Damodar coal; "Ruhr of India"), Meghalaya plateau (Garo/Khasi/Jaintia; Nokrek), Rajmahal–Garo gap (Malda gap).
  • Deccan: lava traps (Cretaceous–Eocene; 5 lakh km²); Western Ghats/Sahyadri (1,600 km; Anamudi 2,695 m highest peninsular — Anaimalai; Doddabetta 2,637 Nilgiri; Kalsubai 1,646 Maharashtra; Kudremukh, Pushpagiri, Mullayanagiri (Karnataka highest 1,930); passes/ghats — Thal (Mumbai–Nashik), Bhor (Mumbai–Pune), Pal (Kolhapur–Ratnagiri), Palakkad/Palghat gap (30 km; Coimbatore–Palakkad), Shencottah/Senkottai (Madurai–Kollam), Goa gap, Amba, Naneghat, Kumbharli; UNESCO 2012; 39 sites; biodiversity hotspot) vs Eastern Ghats (discontinuous; older; Arma Konda/Jindhagada 1,690 AP highest; Mahendragiri (Odisha 1,501), Nallamala (Srisailam; GIB? no—tigers), Palkonda, Velikonda, Seshachalam (Tirumala; red sanders), Javadi, Shevaroy (Yercaud), Kollimalai, Pachaimalai, Nilgiri junction); Nilgiri meet point (Doddabetta; Ooty); Cardamom (Elamalai) & Anaimalai & Palani (Kodaikanal) south of Palghat gap; Deccan plateau proper (Maharashtra, Karnataka (Malnad/Maidan), Telangana), Dandakaranya, Bastar, Garhjat hills (Odisha), Karnataka plateau (Bababudan — iron; Kudremukh; Jog falls on Sharavati).
  • Hills in news: Similipal, Niyamgiri (Dongria Kondh; bauxite), Gandhamardan (bauxite), Nallamala (uranium), Shevaroy, Agasthyamalai (biosphere), Anamalai, Sathyamangalam, Amrabad, Kudremukh (iron mining ban 2005), Aravalli (illegal mining; SC 2024 definition — >100 m), Malwa (Deccan traps), Lonar (meteorite crater lake; Ramsar 2020).

Coasts & islands

  • West coast (narrow; submerged; estuaries; Konkan (Daman–Goa), Kanara/Karavali (Goa–Mangaluru), Malabar (Kerala; kayals/backwaters — Vembanad, Ashtamudi; Kuttanad below sea level); Kutch & Kathiawar (Gujarat; Rann; Gir; Girnar), lagoons, ports natural (Mumbai, Marmagao, Kochi, New Mangalore), high tidal ranges Khambhat); East coast (wide; emergent; deltas — Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri; Utkal (Odisha; Chilika largest brackish lagoon; Bhitarkanika), Northern Circars (AP; Kolleru freshwater lake; Pulicat lagoon — Sriharikota barrier), Coromandel (TN; NE monsoon rain), Pulicat, Point Calimere, Vedaranyam; ports artificial (Chennai, Vizag natural, Paradip, Ennore, Tuticorin); Marina beach; Dhanushkodi.
  • Andaman & Nicobar (572 islands; 37 inhabited; Ten Degree Channel A–N; Duncan Passage (South Andaman–Little Andaman), Coco channel (Myanmar); Saddle Peak 732 m highest (N Andaman); Barren (active), Narcondam; Indira Point; Great Nicobar (Campbell Bay; Galathea — transhipment project); Baratang mud volcano; Cellular jail; Ross → Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep, Neil → Shaheed, Havelock → Swaraj; tribes — Great Andamanese, Onge, Jarawa, Sentinelese (North Sentinel), Shompen (Nicobar), Nicobarese; Car Nicobar; Katchal 2004 tsunami).
  • Lakshadweep (36 islands; 32 km²; coral atolls; 10 inhabited; Minicoy (southernmost; Mahl; Nine Degree Channel separates from rest; Eight Degree Channel — Maldives), Kavaratti capital, Agatti airport, Bangaram, Pitti (bird sanctuary), Bitra smallest; entirely ST; new tourism push 2024).
  • Other: Majuli (river island; Brahmaputra; district 2016), Bhola/Salsette (Mumbai), Diu, Sriharikota (barrier island; Pulicat; SDSC-SHAR), New Moore/Purbasha (disappeared), Pamban/Rameswaram (Adam's bridge/Ram Setu; Pamban bridge new vertical-lift 2024), Elephanta, Vypin, Willingdon (artificial; Kochi), Sagar (Gangasagar), Nachugunta, Katchatheevu (ceded to Sri Lanka 1974; in news 2024), Abdul Kalam (Wheeler; DRDO), St Mary's (basalt columns; Udupi), Netrani, Munroe (Kerala backwaters), Umananda (smallest inhabited river island; Guwahati), Sambhar? (lake, not island).

Traps

  • Highest peak in India: Kangchenjunga (K2 is in PoK-administered Karakoram — official Indian claim lists K2 as highest). Highest wholly in India: Nanda Devi. Highest peninsular: Anamudi (not Doddabetta).
  • Meghalaya plateau is peninsular (not Himalayan) — separated by Malda/Garo–Rajmahal gap.
  • Palghat gap = Western Ghats break (Kerala–TN); Shencottah gap further south.
  • Ten Degree Channel: Andaman–Nicobar; Nine Degree: Lakshadweep–Minicoy; Eight Degree: Minicoy–Maldives.
  • Chilika = largest brackish lagoon; Vembanad = longest lake; Wular = largest freshwater (J&K); Kolleru freshwater (AP); Loktak (phumdis; Manipur); Sambhar largest inland salt lake; Pangong/Tso Moriri high-altitude (Ladakh).

Key Points & Mindmap

Skeleton facts and recall triggers.

Division-anchor flash.

Himalaya flash

  • N→S: Karakoram/Ladakh → Great (Himadri) → Lesser (Himachal) → Siwalik-Dun.
  • India's highest peak → Kanchenjunga (Sikkim) · syntaxial bends → Nanga Parbat + Namcha Barwa.
  • Passes → Zoji la-Banihal (J&K) · Shipki la (HP) · Mana-Niti (Uttarakhand) · Nathu-Jelep (Sikkim) · Bomdi la (Arunachal).

Plains flash

  • Belt order from hills → Bhabar (gravel) → Terai (marsh) → Bhangar (old alluvium) → Khadar (new).
  • Doabs → Bist (Beas-Sutlej), Bari (Ravi-Beas), Rechna (Chenab-Ravi), Chaj (Chenab-Jhelum) · Majuli → Brahmaputra island.

Peninsula flash

  • Aravalli = oldest fold, eroded (Guru Shikhar) · Deccan Traps = flood basalt · Sahyadri continuous-west, E-Ghats discontinuous.
  • Peaks → Anaimudi 2695 (Anaimalai), Doddabetta (Nilgiri), Guru Shikhar (Mount Abu) · gaps → Thal-Bhor, Palghat, Shencottah.
  • Plateaus → Malwa, Chotanagpur (minerals), Meghalaya (Khasi), Chhattisgarh.

Coast-island flash

  • West → Konkan-Kanara-Malabar: narrow, estuaries, kayals · East → Utkal-Coromandel: wide, deltas.
  • Lagoons → Chilika (Odisha), Pulicat (AP-TN), Vembanad (Kerala) · islands → Andaman-Nicobar (volcanic arc), Lakshadweep (atolls).

Desert flash

  • Thar → longitudinal dunes · barchan = crescent · Luni = SW-draining · Rann = salt flats · Indira Gandhi Canal → Sriganganagar belt.

Trap flash

  • Everest is in Nepal; Kanchenjunga = India's highest (Sikkim).
  • Terai = marshy re-emergence (gravel = Bhabar).
  • Palghat gap = between Anaimalai and Palni-Cardamom line (Coimbatore-Palakkad axis).
  • E-Ghats continuity breaks at the Mahanadi-Krishna mouths — 'discontinuous' keyword.
  • Andaman = Arakan-Yoma extension (not coral).
